title: selectiveLogic 'or' is not 'either'; UI has four Logic buttons
reality: docs/lorebooks/entries.md:78-83 lists exactly four Logic buttons: AND Any, AND All, NOT Any (blocked if any secondary key appears), NOT All (blocked only if all secondary keys appear). Code agrees: packages/client/src/components/lorebooks/LorebookEntryRow.tsx:166-171 (SELECTIVE_LOGIC_OPTIONS has and/and_all/not/not_all, no 'or'); packages/shared/src/utils/lorebook-keyword-matching.ts:121-130 ('or' falls through to the same branch as 'and' = at least one secondary); packages/server/src/services/lorebook/keyword-scanner.ts:648-663 (primary keys must match before secondary logic is even checked, so a secondary key alone never activates an entry).
fix: lorebooks.md Entry Fields row selectiveLogic: name the UI buttons (`and` = AND Any, `and_all` = AND All, `not` = NOT Any = blocked if any secondary key appears, `not_all` = NOT All = blocked only if every secondary key appears). Say primary keys must always match; `or` exists only in the schema/importer and behaves exactly like `and` (it is not 'primary OR secondary').

skill_evidence: references/lorebooks.md:45 "`constant` | bool | `false` | **If true, ALWAYS injected** (no keyword needed)." (contradicted by the file's own lines 254 and 313, where constants can be budget-rejected or Decision-gated)

title: Budget trimming order: Constant, then latest-message matches, then Order
skill_evidence: references/lorebooks.md:236 "If more entries match than fit, lower-`order` entries inject first (constant entries and group weighting also factor in)"; :238 "Order and group weighting decide who survives, so `order` is ... the priority list for what gets dropped under pressure."
reality: docs/lorebooks/token-budgets.md:38-46: Constant entries first, then entries that matched the latest message, then normal injection order; a skipped entry does not stop the walk, so a smaller entry below it can still fit. Code agrees: packages/server/src/services/lorebook/index.ts:550-556 lorebookSelectionOrder (constant > matchedCurrentContext > injectionOrder); keyword-scanner.ts:559 and 654-655 (matchedCurrentContext = a primary key matched the latest *user* message) and 774-777 (current semantic matches get the same flag). So a low Order does not beat a Constant or a fresh latest-message match, and sticky/older-match entries are trimmed before them.
fix: lorebooks.md Token Budget Management: replace the order/group sentence with the real tiers: (1) Constant, (2) entries whose keys matched the latest user message, plus current semantic matches, (3) configured Order; each entry that would overflow the lorebook or chat budget is skipped and the walk continues. Say that Order only ranks entries inside a tier. Group lotteries are resolved before budgeting, one winner per group. Cite docs/lorebooks/token-budgets.md 'How entries get trimmed'.

title: `scope` object and chat pinning mis-described as 'chatId + scope = chat targeting'
skill_evidence: references/lorebooks.md:17 "or per-chat (`chatId` / `scope` object)"; :216 "**`chatId`** plus the **`scope`** object `{ mode: "all" | "disabled" | "specific", chatIds: [] }` — chat targeting."; :230 "Current scene state ... → chat-scoped."
reality: docs/lorebooks/overview.md:53-57 gives three activation routes: Global, Linked to a character/persona, and Pinned to a single chat from that chat's settings. docs/lorebooks/linking-to-characters.md:40-50: **Scope** is set in the Assign dialog of a *linked* lorebook, with the modes All chats with [name] (default), Disabled for all chats and Specific chats (at least one chat must be checked). linking-to-characters.md:94: Chat Settings → Lorebooks → **Add Lorebook** pins a lorebook, and it shows a **Chat** badge. Code: packages/server/src/services/storage/lorebooks.storage.ts:822-845 applies `scope` to every enabled lorebook first, then admits it if it is global, pinned via chat metadata `activeLorebookIds`, character- or persona-owned, or owned by `chatId`. lorebook.schema.ts:17-21,171,175.
fix: Rewrite the Scope bullet. `scope` = which chats a lorebook may activate in (UI: Scope in the character/persona Lorebook tab's Assign dialog — All chats with [name] / Disabled for all chats / Specific chats). Per-chat use is **pinning**: Chat Settings → Lorebooks → Add Lorebook, stored in the chat's `activeLorebookIds` (badge **Chat**). `chatId` marks a lorebook owned by one chat. Point 'chat-scoped' advice at Add Lorebook.

title: Regex keys that time out don't match (no plain-text fallback)
skill_evidence: references/lorebooks.md:373 "An invalid or potentially very slow regex key silently falls back to a plain-text match"
reality: docs/lorebooks/entries.md:66: each regex key runs under a short safety timeout, and a pattern that runs too long does not match on that scan. Code: the skill's sentence is right only for invalid or statically unsafe patterns (packages/shared/src/utils/lorebook-keyword-matching.ts:55-66,89-91 fall back to a literal match). A pattern that passes the static check but exceeds the 50 ms runtime limit returns no match and logs a warning, deliberately with no literal fallback (packages/server/src/services/lorebook/regex-timeout.ts:9-13,19,36-45).
fix: lorebooks.md Keyword choice: 'An invalid or ReDoS-shaped regex key falls back to a plain-text match; a pattern that compiles but takes over ~50 ms on the chat text simply doesn't match that scan (a server warning names it). Keep regex keys simple.'
